request.spec:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The tree search is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests: the tree-search test and the three scenario tests.

**How it works**
- **Which sheets it covers:** it walks up the parent chain to the top sheet, then takes that sheet and everything below it. The sheet you're on comes first, in list order; the other sheets follow, sorted by sheet id.
- **What matches:** a person's name or any of their aliases containing the typed text, case ignored. An empty search lists everyone in the tree.
- **The due-total** is taken from each sheet's own figures, the same values written to the audit's `ROLLUP` lines. So it shows `n/a` where no rate applies and changes after a retirement.
- The search only reads data. It writes nothing to the store or the audit file.

**What changed**
- **Server:** a new `search` method in `RollupService.java`, exposed as `GET /api/sheets/{id}/tree/search?name=` in `ConsolidatedController.java`.
- **Front end:** a new component, `features/tree-search/tree-search.ts`, placed on the home screen just above the audit viewer. It uses the test ids `search-name`, `search`, `search-count`, `search-line` and `search-error`. The count clears as soon as you press Search and reappears once the results are in, as the testing rules require.

I didn't trim the search text, so leading or trailing spaces count as part of what you're searching for.

probe.probe_text:
I've finished reading the code; nothing was changed. Here is the answer.

## 1. Figures the sheet shows, and the rules behind them

### Per claim (`claims.ts` template; data from `ClaimController.ClaimView`)

| testid | Figure | Rule (as the code names it) |
|---|---|---|
| `claim-amount` | amount | Up to 2 decimals, between −10 digits and +10 digits. A negative amount is a **correction** (`isCorrection`). It must name a SETTLED claim of the same person in `corrects`, and a positive amount may not name one (`requireCorrection`). Once a claim has **lines**, its amount is Σ qty×unit and can't be edited directly (`addLine`, `ClaimAmountFromLinesException`). |
| `claim-date` | date | Left blank on add, it takes the sheet's `entryDate` if set, otherwise the sheet's `today` (`entryDateOrToday`). Left blank on edit, it takes `today`. It may not fall after the person's `retiredFrom`, or inside a past retirement (`requireClaimable`, `PersonRetirement.bars`). |
| `claim-due-by` | dueBy | Fixed when the claim is **added**: `holidays.businessDaysAfter(date, terms)`. That skips Saturdays, Sundays and the sheet's holidays, and terms of 0 means the date itself. `terms` = the person's own terms, else the grade's `terms-<g>` on the date, else the sheet's `terms` (starting value 14) (`termsFor`). Re-dating or editing never moves it. Adding a holiday later re-works the due-by of every claim that isn't SETTLED or VOID and is due on or after that holiday (`HolidayService`). |
| `claim-period` | period name | The period that contains **dueBy**, not the date. |
| `claim-due` | due | `claimDue` (front end), mirrored by `RollupService.dueOf` / `ClaimService.liveDue`. In order: (1) `settledDue` if it was frozen. (2) Otherwise the **figure**: `statedDue` if `bound` (stated and not PENDING), else `amount × rate%` for the person's grade **on the claim's date**, using the rate in force on that date. That rate is the sheet's own, else a parent's up to `PARENT_LEVELS`=3 up (`rateChain`/`rateOn`), and a rate's `toDate` can end it (`appliesOn`). No rate means **n/a**. The figure is rounded to 2 decimals by `rounding(roundingDate)`: **HALF_UP if roundingDate < policyDate (or today if there is no policy date), else HALF_EVEN**. A correction's `roundingDate` is the date of the claim it corrects. (3) Add the `lateCharge` while the claim is open (OPEN/PENDING) and not deferred. For each full 30 days that today is past `overdueBy` (dueBy + the grade's `grace-<g>` days on the claim's date), add `late-pct` (in force on that boundary date) of figure + earlier charges. It compounds, and each step is rounded the same way. (4) `floored`: max with the `floor` in force on the claim's date (starting value 1.00). A correction gets neither the late charge nor the floor. |
| `claim-overdue` | yes/no | OPEN/PENDING, not deferred, and `overdueBy` < today. |
| `claim-status` | DRAFT→OPEN→SETTLED; PENDING; VOID; DELETED | `ClaimStatus.canMoveTo`. `counts()` = OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED. `isOpen()` = OPEN, PENDING. |
| `claim-number` | number | Given on **open**. If `numbersByPeriod` (today ≥ `periodNumberingFrom`), it's `<period>-n`, or `X-n` when there's no period. Otherwise it's `FYyyyy-n` for the fiscal year of **dueBy**, shared across the whole sheet tree (`nextClaimNumber`). A reassign or transfer gives the claim a new number. A voided claim keeps its number. |
| `claim-stated` | yes/no | Bound by the person's last statement. |
| `claim-deferred` / `-until` | deferral | `deferralRunning`: deferredUntil > today. |
| `claim-late-entry` | yes/no | The claim was added (or split) while its dueBy's period was **soft-closed**. |
| `claim-opened-by`, `claim-batch`, `claim-proofs`, `claim-split-from`, `claim-reminded`, `claim-corrects`, `claim-ref`, `claim-tags`, `claim-void-reason`, `claim-log-line` (status, by, date, due at that moment) | These are stored values. `ref` must be unique on the sheet, ignoring case. Tags are trimmed, lower-cased, de-duplicated and sorted. |

### Per person (`people.ts`)

- **`person-claimed`** (`claimedBy`): the sum of amounts of **live** claims, leaving out corrections.
  - `live` = counts() and not deferred today.
  - An open claim that isn't bound also drops out if it is dated inside a **hold**, or if the person's `retiredFrom` ≤ today (`Person.counts` / `leftOut`).
- **`person-due-total`** (`dueTotalOf`): the sum of the live claims' dues, skipping n/a, then **capped** at the `cap` in force today.
  - It shows **n/a** only when all three are true: the grade in force today has no rate today, no counted claim has a fixed due (`dueFixed`), and no counted claim has a due and is dated ≤ today.
- **`person-excess`**: how far the uncapped total is over the cap.
- **`person-settled-total`**, **`person-open-total`**: the live dues split by status.
- **`person-overdue-count`**, **`person-overdue-total`**: the live claims that are overdue, and their dues.
- **`person-aged-0-30/31-60/61+`**: the dues of open live claims, bucketed by days from the claim's date to today.
- **`person-active`**: has an open live claim dated within the 30 days up to today.
- **`person-backing`**: each patron's SETTLED dues dated in the last 90 days × their share/100, rounded half-even. Shares are 100.00 split equally, half-even, with the remainder going to the first-named patron (`patronShares`).
- **`person-cut-total`** (`pools.ts`): the pot is shared by members' shares, but only in a **balanced** pool (shares total 100.00).
  - Members outside their membership dates are left out entirely.
  - A retired member gets no cut, and neither does a member held **on today**. Their share is spread over the members who do get a cut.
  - A sub-pool gets its parent's cut as its pot.
- **`person-statement-count`**, **`person-stated-total`**, **`person-statement-date`** (`StatementSummary`).
  - Taking a statement (`StatementService.take`) binds every counting claim to its **figure**: the pre-late-charge, pre-floor value. Late charge and floor are still added live afterwards.
  - It unbinds every other claim and records the capped due-total.
  - With an as-of date, it replays statuses from the claim log, rates as they stood then (`rateAsOf`), and holds and retirements as of that date.
  - Only a steward can cancel the last statement, and doing so unbinds all of the person's claims.
- **`person-grade`**: the grade in force today (grades are dated). **`person-terms`**, **`person-retired`/`-from`**, **`person-hold-line`**, **`person-clashing`** (the name or an alias is used elsewhere in the sheet tree), **`person-snapshot-line`** (due-total on each `today` you leave).

### Sheet totals

- `rollup-claimed-total` and the settled/open totals are plain sums.
- **`rollup-due-total`** and **`rollup-overdue-total`** are `trimmedSum`: with 3 or more people, the single highest and the single lowest are left out.
- **Consolidated** figures add up the descendant sheets.
- **Period due-total**:
  - Once the period is closed or soft-closed, it shows the `personTotals` that were frozen then.
  - While it is open, it is the live dues of claims whose **dueBy** is in the period and whose status at the end of the period's to-date (from the claim log) counted (`dueTotalsBetween` / `liveAtEnd`).

### Freezing

- **Settle** freezes `settledDue` = floor(figure + late charge as of today), or the bare figure for a correction. With no rate it stays live (null).
- **Approve** freezes the same way.
- **Resettle** (steward only) re-freezes from today's rates, ignoring any statement.
- A **statement** binds the figure.
- **Closing a period** freezes the per-person totals.

### Who may do what

- **Roles**: a role is clerk, steward or viewer. A name with no role set is a clerk. A delegation that covers today makes the user a steward.
- **Permission matrix**: `Sheet.allows`. The default (`STANDING_PERMISSIONS`) is that open, settle, void and close are clerk+steward, while reassign and reopen are steward only.
- **Viewers**: a viewer may change nothing (`ViewerInterceptor`).
- **Archived sheets**: an archived sheet refuses every change (`ArchivedInterceptor`).
- **Four eyes**: whoever opened or last edited a claim cannot settle or approve it.
- **Clerk limit**: a clerk settling a claim whose live due is above the `clerk-limit` (in force today) sends it to **PENDING** instead. A steward then approves it (settle) or rejects it (back to OPEN, keeping its old statement binding).
- **Steward-only actions**: approve, reject, resettle, redate (OPEN or PENDING only), void a SETTLED claim within `SETTLED_VOID_DAYS`=7 of its last SETTLED log date, cancel a statement, merge, transfer, archive.
- **Threshold checks**:
  - `proof-threshold` (the grade's own `proof-threshold-<g>`, else the sheet's, on the claim's date): above it, a claim can't be settled or approved without a proof.
  - `note-threshold`: above it, a claim can't be opened with an empty note.
- **Period cap**: a period's `cap` limits how many OPEN/PENDING claims each person may have due in it when opening one.
- **Void reasons**: once the sheet has a void-reason list, every void needs a reason from it.

### What a date decides

- Everything uses the **sheet's `today`**, never the real clock.
- The **claim date** picks the grade, the rate, the floor, the grace days, the terms and the thresholds.
- The **dueBy** picks the period, the number sequence and the fiscal year, and it is what closed-period checks test.
- The **roundingDate**, compared against the policy date, picks HALF_UP or HALF_EVEN.
- The **late-pct** is looked up on each 30-day boundary date.
- The **clerk limit and the cap** are looked up on today.
- **Changing today**:
  - It writes a SNAPSHOT of each person's due-total for the day being left.
  - It **auto-closes** every open period whose to-date + `graceDays` is before the new today.
  - It releases all editor locks.

### Closed / soft-closed periods

- **Closed**: `requireOpen(dueBy)` refuses every add, edit, line, lock, delete, restore, status change, defer, reassign, redate, split, proof, resettle and approve/reject for claims due in it.
- **Soft-closed**: freezes the figures but still allows changes. Claims added while it is soft-closed are flagged as `lateEntry` and write `LATE_ENTRY`.
- **Reopen**: makes the period's totals live again.

### Holds, retirement, deferral

- **Hold** (from/to dates): unbound open claims **dated** inside a hold drop out of every live total and out of statements. Pool cuts look at the hold **on today** instead.
- **Retirement**: from the moment `retiredFrom` ≤ today, all of the person's unbound open claims drop out. Claims dated after `retiredFrom` are refused.
- **Deferral** (OPEN only, until a date after today): while it runs, the claim counts in no total, isn't overdue, gets no late charge, can't be settled or split, and isn't bound by a statement.

### Imports and other bulk adds

- **Import people** (`name,grade,terms,contact`) is all-or-nothing.
  - A line whose name matches an existing person (by name or alias) **updates** them. Their grade is recorded **from today**, and their terms and contact are set only if the line gives them.
  - Every other line adds a person.
  - A name or contact repeated within the paste refuses the whole import.
- **Import rates** (`grade,rate,from,to`) is all-or-nothing and replaces any rate with the same from-date.
- **Paste claims** adds DRAFTs all-or-nothing. A note ending in ` #ref` sets the reference.
- **Quick-add** creates a missing person with grade A.
- **Plans** generate a DRAFT claim for each plan date up to today. A refused date is skipped and tried again by the next generate.
- **Bulk settle** is all-or-nothing under one batch number. **Bulk open** goes claim by claim.

## 2. How hard was this to follow?

Quite hard. The due and total logic isn't in one place. It is written at least four times:
- `ClaimService` (`liveDue`, `settle`, `resettle`)
- `RollupService` (`dueOf`, `snapshot`, `dueTotalsBetween`)
- `StatementService` (`take`, `takeAsOf`), which has its own as-of variants
- the Angular front end (`claimDue`, `lateCharge`, `uncappedDueTotalOf`, `liveAtEnd` in `claims.ts`, `people.ts` and `rates.ts`), which is what actually puts the figures on screen

The supporting rules are spread across `Sheet`, `Person`, `ClaimStatus`, `PeriodService` and `HolidayService`. A new developer has to keep all of these copies in step by hand, and the doc comments are often the only thing that says they're meant to agree.
